importance_ranking.reason: Visual variation across container home types is extreme — luxury villa, basic labour accommodation, resort pod, and farmhouse unit are visually worlds apart. Buyers use the image to identify product type and finish level before reading any text; wrong visual = immediate skip.
Layout (1BHK/2BHK) and size (20ft/40ft) are the primary shortlisting criteria — non-interchangeable across buyer requirements. A listing without these specs cannot be evaluated for fit.

Container homes are large capital purchases where Indian buyers compare prices aggressively across sellers after confirming visual and configuration fit. Price varies substantially with layout, size, and finish tier — buyers discover across spec tiers, making this spec-driven rather than commodity pricing.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard 1BHK/2BHK configurations are quoted per unit (complete structure); custom or large-scale builds are quoted per sq ft of built-up area. Both conventions are confirmed in the Indian market — unit must be shown alongside price to prevent comparison errors.
importance_ranking.reason: Per unit vs per sq ft is a confirmed real ambiguity in the Indian container home market. Price cannot be meaningfully compared across listings without knowing the unit basis.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in the Indian container home market — buyers search by configuration and price, not manufacturer name; Karmod, Unostructures, and others are manufacturer names, not brands buyers actively seek by name.
importance_ranking.reason: Manufacturer track record, installation capability, warranty, and delivery scope are evaluated during final vendor selection. Post-sale dependency is high (installation is integral to the product), but company ranks below specs and price in initial shortlisting.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Layout (1 Room / 1BHK / 2BHK) is the primary product class separator — a buyer needing 2BHK cannot substitute a 1 Room unit, and price scales non-linearly across layout tiers.

Wall panel material defines the insulation and build quality tier (basic GI sheet vs PUF/Rockwool insulated panel), driving a significant price delta and determining climate suitability — non-interchangeable across project requirements.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers comparing a basic labour accommodation unit against a luxury container villa need a finish-tier signal — this dimension is explicitly identified as a key buyer decision factor in the Indian market and is not captured by any existing spec.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Container length (20ft/40ft) directly determines the product tier and price — sellers can immediately identify whether they supply the required configuration and quote accurately.
Toilet/bathroom inclusion determines whether wet works fabrication is in scope — a significant cost and lead-time differentiator that sellers need to confirm fit and price before responding.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know the room configuration (1BHK, 2BHK, open studio) to confirm they can supply the required layout and quote accurately — Length alone does not capture whether the buyer wants a single open space or a partitioned multi-room unit.

buyer_spec_thumbnail_prompts.prompt_for_generation: Interior view of a prefabricated mild steel container home configured as 1BHK — a compact separate bedroom with a small living area visible through an open doorway, clean white walls, vinyl flooring, natural light from a window, no people, realistic architectural render style.

Interior view of a prefabricated mild steel container home configured as 2BHK — two separate bedrooms visible with a connecting hallway, clean walls, laminate flooring, natural light, no people, realistic architectural render style showing dual-room layout clearly.

Interior view of a prefabricated mild steel container home in open hall studio configuration — single undivided open space with combined living and sleeping area, no internal partition walls, large window, clean minimal interior, vinyl flooring, no people, realistic architectural render style.

Interior view of a prefabricated mild steel container home with 1 room plus attached toilet — a single room with a clearly visible attached bathroom door in the corner, compact layout, clean walls, basic flooring, no people, realistic architectural render style showing the toilet attachment clearly.
